problem: The staged-update flow originally shelled out to system tar via execSync to extract the GitHub release tarball. On Windows where Git for Windows puts GNU tar first in PATH, GNU tar misinterprets drive-letter paths (C:\...) as remote host syntax, making hlx update fail. The current branch already replaces the shell-based tar call with an in-process JavaScript tar extraction (src/update/extract.ts) using only Node.js built-ins. However, src/update/perform.ts still shells out to xcopy/cp-R via execSync for its EXDEV (cross-filesystem rename) fallback in copyDirRecursive. The user's continuation context requests incorporating a robustness fix that replaces copyDirRecursive's execSync with fs.cpSync and adding perform.test.ts. Neither change is present in the current code.
